answer: Proposal: scoring weight requires a nullifier from a one-per-person anonymous credential; the ledger rejects duplicate nullifiers each epoch. An audited issuer vets unique personhood and issues unlinkable credentials. A nebula of fresh keys maps to one nullifier, so weight never exceeds its zenith of one. More weight means buying real people's credentials: linear cost, deterring only while price plus revocation risk tops capped marginal reward. Weakest trellis rung: the issuer; capture or black markets break the one-per-person rule.
